verdict.rationale: The docs say you can "page through the catalog" of processes, with cursor-based pagination via `nextCursor`. `ultrametric init --dry-run` also previews the selected skill files before writing them, so some browsing before installing is supported. However, this is a thinly described first-party process catalog rather than a clearly documented skills registry or marketplace. Missing for 10: search or filtering of the catalog, a registry, leaderboard or marketplace-style listing with metadata, detailed docs on what catalog entries show, and independent or hands-on corroboration. [2026-10-14 adversarial bias audit (owner-product refresh lane): reverted partial 5 -> none 0, restoring the 2026-10-08 audit: the story object is a browsable, searchable catalog of skills, and the rationale still concedes the cited catalog is "a thinly described first-party process catalog rather than a clearly documented skills registry" with no search or filtering. The only new evidence since the audit is nextCursor pagination of the same process catalog, which addresses neither the object mismatch nor the conceded absence. Ultrametric-affiliation governance, README §9.]
